data.narrative:
Humans& is an AI & Software company at an undisclosed stage with five founders (Eric Zelikman, Georges Harik, Noah Goodman, Andi Peng, Yuchen He). The target operates within a sector containing 16 identified peers, of which 1 trades publicly (Palantir, PLTR) and 8 are private, including Figure AI, Scale AI, Waymo, and Reflection AI.

The peer-median method is not applicable here. While 16 same-sector comparables exist, filtering by stage, adjacency, and valuation tier yielded fewer than three datapoints—the minimum threshold for robust triangulation. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable methodological noise given the heterogeneity of business models, maturity stages, and capital intensity across the broader AI & Software universe.

The absence of a sufficient tight peer set, combined with undisclosed funding history and current valuation, precludes a quantitative triangulated range at this time. A credible valuation would require either: (1) disclosure of stage and recent funding round details to enable stage-appropriate peer filtering, or (2) expansion of the comparable universe through identification of additional private peers with publicly disclosed valuations. The single public comparable (Palantir) offers limited insight without stage alignment and company-specific operating metrics. Further diligence on Humans&'s revenue, user metrics, or recent fundraising terms is necessary to establish an evidence-based valuation range.
